answer: Each agent identity must lock a slashable bond before it can transact or vote, like staking a plot in a shared garden: one plot, one bond. Creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds, so attack cost grows linearly while honest agents pay once. Misbehavior proven by peers burns the bond. A vine can spread cheaply, but velvet gloves cannot hide that every new hand must post real collateral first.
